# AI Model Capability Benchmark Data

## Overview
Normalized benchmark scores for 10 large language models across 8 capability dimensions, designed for parallel coordinates visualization. Models span 5 families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen) with both flagship and lightweight variants per family.

## Data Source

### model_benchmarks
Each record represents one AI model with the following fields:
- **model** (string): Model name, e.g., "GPT-4o", "Claude 3.5 Sonnet"
- **family** (string): Model family grouping — one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen
- **Reasoning** (integer, 0-100): Complex multi-step reasoning benchmark score
- **Code Generation** (integer, 0-100): Programming and code synthesis score
- **Math / Quantitative** (integer, 0-100): Mathematical problem-solving score
- **Language Understanding** (integer, 0-100): NLU and reading comprehension score
- **Multimodal Understanding** (integer, 0-100): Image, video, and cross-modal reasoning score
- **Instruction Following** (integer, 0-100): Adherence to complex user instructions
- **Inference Speed** (integer, 0-100): Normalized throughput (higher = faster)
- **Knowledge Recall** (integer, 0-100): Factual knowledge and world knowledge retrieval

All scores are normalized to a 0-100 scale for cross-dimension comparability.

## Data Notes
- Scores are synthetic composites inspired by publicly reported benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, MMMU, MT-Bench, etc.) but do not correspond to exact published numbers.
- Inference Speed is inversely related to model size; lightweight variants score higher.
- Multimodal scores for text-only-focused models (LLaMA, Qwen) are notably lower, reflecting limited native multimodal capability.
- Each family includes one flagship and one smaller/faster variant to illustrate capability-efficiency trade-offs.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open("/app/benchmark/source_data.json") as f:
    source = json.load(f)

data = source["model_benchmarks"]["data"]

# Axis order to emphasize trade-offs:
# Reasoning ↔ Inference Speed (adjacent), Math/Quantitative ↔ Multimodal Understanding (adjacent)
dimensions = [
    "Reasoning",
    "Inference Speed",
    "Math / Quantitative",
    "Multimodal Understanding",
    "Code Generation",
    "Language Understanding",
    "Instruction Following",
    "Knowledge Recall",
]

# Family color mapping
family_colors = {
    "GPT": "#2563EB",      # blue
    "Claude": "#7C3AED",   # purple
    "Gemini": "#16A34A",   # green
    "LLaMA": "#EA580C",    # orange
    "Qwen": "#DC2626",     # red
}

# Compute average score per model to determine line prominence
for m in data:
    scores = [m[d] for d in dimensions]
    m["avg"] = np.mean(scores)

avg_scores = [m["avg"] for m in data]
avg_threshold = np.percentile(avg_scores, 70)  # top ~30% get prominent lines

# Figure setup
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9), dpi=150)
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")
ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

n_axes = len(dimensions)
x_positions = np.arange(n_axes)

# Plot each model's polyline
for m in data:
    y_vals = [m[d] for d in dimensions]
    color = family_colors[m["family"]]
    is_top = m["avg"] >= avg_threshold
    lw = 2.8 if is_top else 1.0
    alpha = 0.95 if is_top else 0.45
    zorder = 10 if is_top else 3

    ax.plot(x_positions, y_vals, color=color, linewidth=lw, alpha=alpha, zorder=zorder,
            label=m["family"] if is_top else None, solid_capstyle="round")

    # Add model name at the end for top models
    if is_top:
        ax.text(x_positions[-1] + 0.12, y_vals[-1], m["model"],
                fontsize=7.5, fontweight="bold", color=color, va="center", zorder=15)

# Draw vertical axes
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color="#D1D5DB", linewidth=1.2, zorder=1)
    ax.text(i, 101, dim, ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold",
            color="#374151", rotation=25)

    # Tick labels on each axis
    for tick_val in [20, 40, 60, 80, 100]:
        ax.text(i, tick_val, str(tick_val), ha="center", va="center",
                fontsize=6.5, color="#9CA3AF", zorder=2)

# Axis limits
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, n_axes - 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(25, 108)

# Remove default axes
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Title
ax.set_title("AI Model Capability Profiles: Parallel Coordinates View",
             fontsize=16, fontweight="bold", color="#111827", pad=30)

# Subtitle
ax.text(0.5, 1.04, "Each line represents one model across 8 benchmark dimensions  |  "
        "Line thickness indicates overall performance tier  |  "
        "Color encodes model family",
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#6B7280", style="italic")

# Annotation: Reasoning ↔ Speed tradeoff
mid_x_rs = 0.5
ax.annotate("Reasoning ↔ Speed\ntradeoff visible:\nhigh reasoning → low speed",
            xy=(mid_x_rs, 58), fontsize=7.5, color="#6B7280",
            ha="center", va="center",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="#FEF3C7", edgecolor="#F59E0B", alpha=0.85),
            zorder=20)

# Annotation: Math ↔ Multimodal divergence
mid_x_mm = 2.5
ax.annotate("Math ↔ Multimodal\ndivergence: models\nstrong in one dip in the other",
            xy=(mid_x_mm, 52), fontsize=7.5, color="#6B7280",
            ha="center", va="center",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="#DBEAFE", edgecolor="#3B82F6", alpha=0.85),
            zorder=20)

# Legend — one entry per family
legend_handles = []
for family, color in family_colors.items():
    # Two entries: thick (flagship) and thin (lightweight)
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    legend_handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], color=color, linewidth=2.5, alpha=0.95,
                                  label=f"{family} (flagship)"))
    legend_handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], color=color, linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.45,
                                  label=f"{family} (lightweight)"))

legend = ax.legend(handles=legend_handles, loc="lower center", ncol=5, fontsize=8,
                   frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#D1D5DB",
                   title="Model Family  ─  Line Thickness = Performance Tier",
                   title_fontsize=8.5)
legend.get_title().set_fontweight("bold")

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
plt.close()
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
